what_worked.multi_segment_load: the platform reported both segments and issued one writemem per segment
what_worked.execution: the graph ran to completion: [nr] RA returned: PASS, verify NR runtime: PASS

what_is_wrong.verdict: the graph executes on the board but the numbers are wrong; this is NOT a passing numeric result
what_is_wrong.board_logit_note: 0x00400000 is a denormal, not 2.0. The winning logit is essentially zero, so the logits are not the reference's order of magnitude (~30) at all.

suspects_not_yet_excluded: the 685 MB writemem may be truncated or wrapped by the RTL DDR model: the operator examples only ever touched a few KB at 0xb8000000, so a 653 MiB write into i_ddr[25387219:14680064] has never been exercised before
the model main's descriptors point at .workspace; the linker places them at 0xb8000000 only if they are the first .workspace items, which has not been verified on hardware
the graph's parameter order and the segment's section order are assumed to agree; run_graph_host.py checks that against the layout, but nothing checks it against the segment file
next_diagnostic: print a checksum over a slice of the parameter buffer and the first few embedding values from the board, and compare with the same values computed from the segment file locally; that separates 'segment did not arrive' from 'graph read it wrong'

infrastructure_changes_this_round.fpga_run.py: additive --layout-plan / --segment options that upload the plan and its extra files; the single-image flow is unchanged
